Could your team name every remote path into the environment?

Remote access grows one exception at a time: an employee VPN, a vendor connection, an administrator tunnel, or a link between sites. Each path may be reasonable, but the collection becomes difficult to govern when ownership and review dates are unclear.

At Cloud2e, Edge Transport & Network Engineering starts by mapping topology, rulebases, and dependencies. The service can include firewall management, secure VPN or zero-trust access with device posture checks, segmentation, multi-site connectivity, monitoring, and change control. The intended benefit is a network whose access paths are visible, documented, and operated consistently.

Build a short inventory for each path: business owner, approved users, source device expectations, destination, authentication method, logging, reviewer, and expiration date. Then compare the inventory with the actual configuration.

A remote-access rule should not become permanent simply because nobody remembers why it exists.

Remote access is part of network architecture, not an exception list.

Every employee VPN, vendor connection, administrator path, and site-to-site link should have a defined purpose, owner, permitted destination, authentication method, monitoring plan, and review date. Without that context, old access can remain active long after the business need changes.

Cloud2e's Edge Transport & Network Engineering service includes documented network mapping, firewall architecture and management, secure remote access, segmentation engineering, multi-site connectivity, monitoring, and ongoing change control. This connects remote-access decisions with the broader network design instead of managing each rule in isolation.

A practical review starts with three comparisons:
- documented access paths versus current configurations
- authorized users and devices versus actual use
- temporary approvals versus expiration dates

Resolve the differences, record the decision, and assign the next review. A visible access-path inventory gives IT and business owners a shared picture of how people and systems enter the environment.
